title: Pin Release Tether Checklist (personal scratch)
content:
Goal: quick, low-friction notes for a pinned-canary rollout + a reversible unpin path. Not for sharing as-is; rough thinking.

High-level constraints:
- avoid client-wide sudden flips (no global toggles that affect >5% traffic at once)
- must be reversible within 5 minutes from detection to full rollback for critical errors
- maintain warm caches for top 50 tenants during pin transitions

Definitions (for these notes):
- pin: routing traffic to a fixed model version for a tenant or cohort
- tether: ephemeral routing rule that keeps a small anchored fraction at previous version while majority moves on (safety net)

Preflight checklist (short):
- [ ] baseline perf capture: last 24h P50/P90/P99 latency and error rates for each model variant (scripts/telemetry/collect_baseline.sh)
- [ ] smoke tests green in staging (regressions + auth)
- [ ] identify top-50 tenants and mark as keep-warm candidates (tag in ops-config)
- [ ] confirm alerting thresholds live in pagerduty rule set (alerts: model-edge-error-rate, tok_failure_rate, latency_spike)
- [ ] ensure fallback variant registered and health-checked (fallback=quantized-v2-small)

Traffic plan (example):
- wave 0: 0.5% traffic for 15m (sanity + telemetry)
- wave 1: 2% for 30m (verify latency and hallucination metrics on eval-suite-quick)
- wave 2: 10% for 60m (warm caches, monitor throughput)
- wave 3: 40% for 90m (if green proceed)
- final: 100% after 2h green or do staggered per-region ramp (EU/US/APAC)

Tether strategy (novel):
- when moving a tenant from vA -> vB, attach a 2% tether that pins a small fraction to vA for 12 hours. Purpose: capture tail hits and long-lived contexts that might otherwise be broken by immediate global flip.
- tether is updated with a TTL and auto-evicts after X cycles unless explicitly extended.
- operational notes: implement tether in routing layer as a secondary key (tenant_id mod 50 == tether_bucket) so deterministic assignment.

Rollback triggers (explicit):
- error_rate delta > 0.75% absolute over baseline and sustained for 3 consecutive 5m windows
- P99 latency increases > 40% and impacts >10% of requests in last 10m
- semantic eval score drop (eval-suite-critical) by >= 7 pts on new prompts
- customer escalation with P1 tag (immediate rollback)

Quick command crib (for myself):
- view cohort assignment: kubectl exec -it router-prod -- curl localhost:9090/cohorts?tenant=TENANT_ID
- apply a tether: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ME" $OPS_API/tethers -d '{"tenant":"T","from":"vA","pct":2,"ttl":"12h"}'  # use jq to template
- pin override: opsctl routes set --tenant T --model vB --reason "pin-for-bugfix-2026-02" --expires 72h
- emergency rollback: opsctl routes set --tenant T --model vA --force --reason "rollback-triggered"

Observability: what to watch in first 90m (dashboard panels I expect to flip):
- request_per_min, error_count, tok_allocate_errors, downstream-queue-length, kv-cache-hit-rate (per-tenant), model-variant-memory-evictions
- logging: correlate trace_id with model_variant tag and cohort tag

Customer-facing considerations:
- if top-5 tenants impacted, prepare a short note: "We've detected X regression in a small fraction of traffic while validating a model update. We have rolled back the affected traffic and continue to investigate. We'll follow up with a timeline."
- handoff to CS: copy / include runbook snippet and head of eng on thread.

Open questions / TODOs (me):
- should tethers be sticky across redeploys? Right now they are not. Pros: short-lived safety. Cons: a tenant might end up tethered repeatedly during subsequent flips.
- how to automatically reconcile warm caches when a tenant is pinned for >24h (thundering rebuilds risk)
- finalize the numeric thresholds for P99 delta (is 40% too aggressive?)

Post-mortem skeleton (if a rollback happens):
- timeline of events (timestamps + who executed what)
- alert channels and paging behavior (who got paged when)
- root cause hypothesis + evidence (traces, logs, eval outputs)
- mitigation steps taken and followups (owner + due dates)

Personal notes (random):
- keep the initial tether small; it's often enough to catch stateful weirdness that global toggles miss.
- prefer deterministic tether assignment over random sampling for easier repro.
- remind SRE to pre-warm the ALB routing caches 30m before wave 2.

End of scratchpad. Will formalize into a short playbook if this approach looks promising after a couple of trials.
